name: Sunday Times cryptic crossword, Penguin book 1 No 76

clue.text: Prospective companions you’ve. never met give you obscure fruit
Twice I appeared before the bird
Indicated danger — and the tree collapsed
One obvious mark of a housewife’s careful management
Hidden and protected as a matter of policy
Love this wing — would that be your view?
‘Every gift of noble — Is breathed upon by Hope’s per- petual breath’ (Wordsworth: National Independence and Liberty)
Origin of the preacher’s text both refers to a religious order and veers away from it
Trouble with the navy’s decks?
A resolute initial approach to all others will cause ap- prehension
High-chairs? Others will certainly be involved about a particular point of definition
One quite socially acceptable metal is returned
Feel fit — net result of one’s splendid condition!
Does it go to the head of the company doctor?
Photograph a monster in your garden, perhaps
‘Come, my friends, ’Tis not too — to seek a newer world’ (Tennyson: Ulysses)
Standard confused before afternoon?
Approach in progress with an indefinite result first
Gay show but impoverished?
Endless street twisting toward a circle. Is that a record?
Drawing together a fastener on a new net
Source of bloomers behind the house
Taming a son leads to hostility
Pleased to study temporary housing
Motorists in clubs?
In order to have the capacity to strike hard, put a drink in your bag
Going south, hikes all over the place to find the chiefs
I need a change from Virgil
Hothead found in a group of secret nationalists?
Nothing is cold!
